title: From slope to a working optimizer
goal: Explain, implement, and diagnose gradient descent on a small quadratic loss.
assumptions: Can rearrange equations and read basic Python.
Single-variable derivative knowledge is unverified; begin with a brief check.
Suggested modules fit several short sessions; revise timing from learner evidence.

modules.title: Slope as local change
modules.outcome: Predict the sign and approximate size of a local function change.
modules.subject: math

assessment.prompt: For f(x)=x^2 at x=2, predict the change for a small positive and negative step.
success_criteria: Relates sign to step direction and labels approximation.

modules.title: Vectors and directional change
modules.outcome: Explain a dot product as the first-order change along a step.
modules.subject: math

assessment.prompt: With gradient (2,4), compare unit steps (1,0) and (0,1).

source_sections.mit-multivariable: Unit 2, Part B: Chain Rule, Gradient and Directional Derivatives

modules.title: What the gradient tells us
modules.outcome: Compute the gradient of x^2+2y^2 and identify a local descent direction.
modules.subject: math

assessment.prompt: At (1,1), compute the gradient and a direction with negative directional derivative.
success_criteria: Explains that the local prediction is first-order.

source_sections.mit-multivariable: Unit 2, Part B: Chain Rule, Gradient and Directional Derivatives

modules.title: One update, then another
modules.outcome: Implement an update and trace the actual loss change.
modules.subject: computer-science

assessment.prompt: Write one gradient step for x^2+2y^2 from (1,1) with eta=0.1.
success_criteria: Updates both coordinates using the old point.

source_sections.mit-gradient-descent: 3.1 Gradient descent in one dimension; 3.2 Multiple dimensions

modules.title: When the step goes too far
modules.outcome: Show how step size changes convergence for f(x)=x^2.
modules.subject: math

assessment.prompt: For x_next=(1-2*eta)*x, find the eta interval giving convergence from nonzero x.

source_sections.mit-gradient-descent: 3.1 Gradient descent in one dimension; 3.2 Multiple dimensions

modules.title: Build and diagnose the optimizer
modules.outcome: Run a small solver, inspect its trace, and explain a failing step size.
modules.subject: computer-science

assessment.prompt: Implement gradient descent on x^2+2y^2; compare eta=0.1 and eta=0.6 from (1,1).
success_criteria: Explains divergence in the y coordinate for eta=0.6.
Reports stopping criterion and distinguishes tolerance from exact optimum.
